title: Natural finite pullback comparison of strict reduction towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ use the small pro-etale site, the completed ring sheaf $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/t^n)_W$, the constant quotient sheaves $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$ and the unbounded derived category $D(R_W)$ of sheaves of $R_W$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All quotient modules are restricted to $R_W$ along the specified limit projections. Let $g:T'\to T$ be any morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Write $c_g:g^{-1}R_T\to R_{T'}$ for the map induced by the finite projections and $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}R_{T'}$ for ordinary ringed-topos module pullback. Use the strict reduction functor $K\mapsto K_\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and the derived strict tower pullback $V_g=Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K\in D(R_T)$ put $P_n=P\otimes_{R_T}S_{T,n}$ and
$$B_g(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*P_n,$$
with the actual quotient transitions; $g_n^*$ is the exact finite-coefficient module pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. This strict tower construction descends to a functor $B_g:D(R_T)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}_{R_{T'}})$, and there is a natural isomorphism of functors
$$b_g:V_g\circ(-)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g.$$
Its specified value on $P$ is represented by the strict-tower zigzag
$$G(P\otimes Q_{T,\bullet})\xrightarrow{\sim}(GP\otimes Q_{T',n})_n\longrightarrow(GP\otimes S_{T',n})_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g(P),$$
where $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$, transition $(t,1)$, and the middle arrow is the quotient augmentation. Here $GP$ and every $G(P\otimes Q_{T,n})$ are K-flat with flat terms and the middle arrow is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. The last arrow is the balanced isomorphism identifying both sides with $g^{-1}P\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}S_{T',n}$; on tensor sections it sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes\bar b a$, with inverse inserting $1$. All scalar maps are the components of $c_g$, so these are exactly the finite evaluation comparisons fixed in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-a1-integral-completed-pullback-interfaces]. For each $r\in\mathbf Z$ these maps commute with the standard termwise tensor and pullback shifts, and hence
$$s^B_{K,r}\circ b_{g,K[r]}=b_{g,K}[r]\circ s^V_{K,r},$$
where $s^V:V_g((K[r])_\bullet)\to V_g(K_\bullet)[r]$ and $s^B:B_g(K[r])\to B_g(K)[r]$ are the reduction/tower-pullback and finite termwise shift comparisons, respectively. The naturality is for all derived morphisms and is independent of representatives, without assuming that $c_g$ is invertible or that $G$ is exact.

proof.text: The preceding three lemmas give chain-map naturality: every local formula replaces $x$ by $g^{-1}f(x)$ on either path, and the augmentation is $1\otimes\epsilon_n$. Using $\chi_P$ and the inverse of the $B_g$ computation gives a natural isomorphism on the homotopy category of good complexes. The flat-term K-flat localization equivalence extends it uniquely to $b_g$ on $D(R_T)$. Explicitly the naturality equation for a resolving quasi-isomorphism $s$ can be multiplied by its two invertible functor images to give naturality for $s^{-1}$; localized chain maps give every derived morphism. Every object has a good representative, so every component is invertible. This proves independence of representatives; all components are $R_{T\prime}$-linear by the balanced formulas.

proof.text: For $r\in\mathbf Z$, extracting the first-variable shift from $P[r]\otimes Q_n$ is unsigned by the total-tensor shift lemma. If $x$ has degree $p$ in $P[r]$, both differentials are $(-1)^r dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$, since $(-1)^r(-1)^{p+r}=(-1)^p$. The same holds with $S_n[0]$. Termwise $G$ and $g_n^*$ commute with shifts by identities on terms; the generator formulas, augmentations and transitions have degree zero. Thus every arrow of the zigzag commutes with these shifts. Good complexes are shift-stable: flat terms are reindexed and tensoring with an acyclic complex is merely shifted. The canonical derived reduction and tower-pullback shift comparisons are these termwise comparisons through the resolving counits. Consequently $s^B_{K,r}b_{g,K[r]}=b_{g,K}[r]s^V_{K,r}$ on good representatives. The localization equivalence extends this equation to all $K$.
